title: Restoring Legacy Archival Sports Footage
business: Digital media restoration firms managing historical sports archives.
problem: Legacy footage often suffers from low temporal resolution, resulting in jerky, stuttering motion that appears unnatural when viewed on modern high-refresh-rate displays.
solution: Video Frame Interpolation (VFI) uses convolutional neural networks to synthesize intermediate frames between existing ones, effectively increasing the temporal sampling rate to create smooth, fluid motion without requiring original high-speed camera captures.
steps: Input two consecutive frames into a U-Net architecture to compute initial bi-directional optical flow.
Linearly combine these flows at specific time intervals to approximate intermediate motion paths.
Utilize a secondary U-Net to refine the approximated flow and generate soft visibility maps to handle occlusions.
Warp the original input frames based on the refined flow and visibility masks.
Perform linear fusion of the warped frames to produce the final, temporally coherent intermediate frame.
outcome: The archival footage achieves a fluid, high-frame-rate appearance that matches modern visual standards while maintaining spatial consistency.
limitation: The primary limitation is the generation of artifacts around motion boundaries where occlusion reasoning fails; this can be checked by inspecting the visibility maps for high-error regions during rapid, complex object movement.
